subject: Millcross
prompt: A small, wall-less crossing town of a few dozen structures on both banks of a grey river, viewed from the road at cart height, late afternoon. A queue of wooden ox-carts loaded with sacks, and led pack animals, fills the well-worn earth road from the foreground to the ford, longer than the town is wide — the nearest cart close enough to see the driver walking beside the wheel. One mill-wheel housing stands over the ford, a great wooden wheel turning in the race at its side — the only structure above one storey; everything else is single-storey and solidly built: timber-framed houses with plastered walls on stone footings, steep shingled roofs and real chimneys, ranged in tidy rows along the hard-packed earth roads on both banks. The last house stands in open plain — beyond the town edge only the two earth roads, the ford and low farmland remain. Palette ash-grey, rope-brown, tallow-yellow; the leading awnings chalked with a circle crossed by two strokes.
_promptNote: F-039 (2026-08-08): the phrase "laid out with no plan along the roads" was restated as an assertion. A diffusion text encoder attends to tokens and has no operator for negation, so the old wording delivered `plan` into the conditioning. generate/prompt-lint.mjs now refuses to queue a positive prompt containing negation. F-039 (2026-08-25): "sprawling"/"sprawled" carried no extent bound and every strength-ladder cell tiled shanties to the horizon, while town-millcross.json holds a few dozen placed footprints — the prompt now bounds the count ("a few dozen structures"), asserts the town edge ("beyond the town edge only the two roads...") and declares both via `mustAssert`, enforced by prompt-lint R3/R4. `masses`, horizon, focal, width and height are untouched -- the F-026 depth-map replication record still applies to the control image.
_note: Newly authored to the recovered block-in schema (ABP-flux-dev-and-anchor.md) for this subject — the ABPs only ever block-in'd Gildmark and Norhollow. Also raised land-region coverage (was ~1/3 of the non-sky frame) by widening the town rows to near-full width and adding a mudflat/tent bridge across the former centre gap; sky above the horizon (0.62) is left black on purpose. Composition unchanged in kind: far bank/river on bg right at the horizon, single-storey plank rows + the one taller mill-wheel housing on mg (asymmetric — right bank denser, matching 'longer than the town is wide'), cart queue + led animals occluding the foreground.
